title.narrative: Improving Water-related Disaster Risk Management to Strengthen Climate and Disaster Resilience in Iran

description.narrative: Iran is home to six major basins at Level 1 and 30 basins at Level 2, spanning across 31 provinces. While significant progress is being made in implementing water conservation measures, there is a continued need for greater focus and investment to strengthen expertise and technical capabilities in water-related disaster risk assessment. This project aims to develop flood inundation mapping and flood risk assessments to enhance early warning systems, alongside analyzing extreme hydrological events such as floods and droughts. Drought risk assessments will also be a key component to address water-related disaster risks more effectively. Drawing on Japan's expertise in climate risk resilience, the project seeks to promote proactive water-related disaster risk management and improve emergency response systems. Furthermore, the project adheres to UNESCO's Gender Equality Marker (GEM) standards, setting quotas for women's participation to ensure that their specific vulnerabilities in both urban and rural areas are addressed through targeted measures.
